claims.claim: Anthropic's Punit Shah said ~650 projects applied to OSS Scanner, 114 were accepted, and 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings were reported, with not all projects scanned yet.
OSS Scanner launched on 2026-10-08 and its reports are fully model-generated without human review or triage, produced by models including Claude Mythos.
Anthropic's pilot audit found 85 of 97 critical and high scanner findings across 48 projects (88%) met its CVD bar; 11 were real duplicates and 1 was invalid.
Anthropic acknowledges severity ratings can be inflated or the scanner can misunderstand a project's threat model.
Anthropic's CVD policy says every report it sends generally reflects a finding a human security researcher has reviewed and confirmed.

Anthropic's CVD dashboard listed 29,439 candidates, 6,123 reviewed by external firms, 5,674 confirmed valid (92.7%), 6,157 reported across 591 projects of which 4,824 went direct and may contain false positives, and 516 patched upstream.
The dashboard reports 83.0% exact and 97.1% within-one-band severity agreement between Claude and external firms over 1,337 findings.
Echo found that among 27 Mythos findings that became CVEs, Mythos rated 8 Critical but only one Critical rating held; 13 of 14 mismatches were overstated.
VulnCheck found Claude rated 91.5% of ledger findings critical or high versus 51.3% for maintainers, and the ledger showed 202 fixes versus 421 claimed.
Echo reported 21,119 of 23,019 Mythos candidates had not been reviewed by anyone outside Anthropic and the reviewed set was probably not random.
curl CVE-2026-92392 is an HTTP/2 upload use-after-free rated High, affecting 8.12.0-8.22.0, fixed in 8.23.0, reported 2026-09-15 and credited to Luna with Claude, Anthropic.
Stenberg wrote that the most likely outcome of an attempted attack on CVE-2026-92392 is just a crash; code execution requires precise build and heap knowledge and allows about 23 bytes.
curl, PostgreSQL and the Linux kernel are not in the anthropics/oss-scanner projects directory, which held 128 entries; 845 PRs were filed, 144 merged and 468 closed unmerged.
Of 33 curl CVEs in the September-October 2026 release batches, Aisle Research was credited on 24 and Anthropic on 2.
Pion's maintainer received a report of 36 bugs including 6 security vulnerabilities (2 critical, 3 high, 1 moderate) and triaged them manually after Claude and Codex refused to help.
curl will move LOW and MEDIUM vulnerability reports to public GitHub issues from 2026-10-26 because maintainers are overloaded; over 90% of submissions are below HIGH.
curl's security report rate in 2026 was 4-5 times the 2024 rate and double 2025, while the confirmed rate recovered to about 15-16% after falling below 5% in 2025.
OSS-Fuzz files bugs automatically and verifies fixes automatically, and had helped identify and fix over 13,000 vulnerabilities and 50,000 bugs across 1,000 projects.
CVE records published per year rose from 14,274 in 2020 to 47,803 in 2025 and 81,927 in 2026 through 2026-10-19.
NIST said CVE submissions rose 263% between 2020 and 2025 and moved backlogged CVEs published before 2026-03-01 to Not Scheduled.
DARPA AIxCC finalists found 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities and patched 43, and found 18 real zero-days with 11 patched.
In 2024, NVD rated 13.7% of CVEs Critical and 33.5% High.
Tidelift's 2024 survey found 60% of maintainers are unpaid hobbyists and security work rose from 4% to 11% of their time since 2021.
At the Mythos Preview launch, expert contractors agreed exactly with Claude's severity in 89% of 198 manually reviewed reports.
wolfSSL said all but two of 74 reports it received were valid and five became CVEs.
Stenberg called a third-party Mythos scan of curl in May 2026 an amazingly successful marketing stunt after five confirmed vulnerabilities reduced to one Low CVE.
